about: How many US adults take part in each kind of group, the check for src/core2/modules/groups.ts. The 2017-2023 Civic Engagement and Volunteering supplements ask only whether a person belonged to any group; the last supplement to ask by group type is November 2013.

sources.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Current Population Survey, November 2013 Civic Engagement Supplement, public-use microdata (nov13pub.dat.gz) and codebook (cpsnov13.pdf, Attachment 7, items PES5a-e, columns 959-968); adults 18 and over (38,601), weighted by PWNRWGT; base is yes plus no answers. OPUS-PEOPLE's tabulation; the school and neighborhood share (13.9%) matches Pew's published 13.7% (Pew Research Center 2018, Appendix D).
sources.note: Parent status (PRCHLD) is defined only for the family reference person or spouse.

sources.citation: AmeriCorps, 2017-2023 CEV Findings, National Rates (data.americorps.gov/d/rhng-qtzw), Organizational Membership Rate, ages 16+: 27.1% (2017), 27.1% (2019), 23.8% (2021), 24.9% (2023). One direct question about belonging, so lower than 2013's five prompts by type.

Pew Research Center, Religious Landscape Study 2023-24 (Feb 26, 2025): 33% attend in person at least monthly, 25% weekly, 37% members of a congregation. Gallup 2021-23: weekly 21%, almost weekly 9%, about monthly 11%; church membership 45% (Gallup, 'How Religious Are Americans?', Mar 29, 2024).

Pew Research Center, 'Voters Rarely Switch Parties' (Aug 4, 2020), American Trends Panel, 11,077 registered voters, Sept 2018 to July 2020, leaners counted with their party: 9% of 2018 Republicans and 9% of 2018 Democrats had moved to the other party by 2020; about 8 in 10 gave the same answer in all five surveys. No verified one-year rate.
